claim: Both saved plugin paths render the same lazy ESM export oe. It reads plugin/tool params, builds and parses an encoded codex://plugins/.../app/... link with search/hash, rejects a disabled inventory capability or invalid link, safely parses location state, and selects global/settings plus target overrides. The component key uses account/user/plugin/tool/entrypoint, not target.

Deep-link resolution separates app-server views from hosted plugin entrypoints. Installed, enabled and admin-availability checks, unique-name fallback, sourceMcpApp matching, settings/global entrypoints and normalized app identities remain distinct. Paths are deduplicated; the result is loading, found, not-found or ambiguous. The app-server branch may query plugin details only after inventory/view loading finishes and a selected plugin lacks a view.

The deep-link presenter shows loading; found returns replacement navigation, spreads existing route state and sets mcpHistoryNavigation=false, entrypoint and mcpAppDeepLink. Ambiguous or completed activation recovery shows the unavailable component. Otherwise it delegates activation to G; completion sets local loading, awaits optional refresh with a no-op catch, then marks complete. This does not prove activation or refresh succeeded.

The shared global-view wrapper reads hostId from search with local default. Only a hosted host uses the supplied hostedView; another host renders rt, which reads host views and passes them to the already-qualified K renderer. Without a persistent workspace it also mounts the header/layout. This host choice is independent of ft productContext.

The imported initial vbn port is aMn. Its complete initializer sets iMn=connector_openai_code_review and aMn=qh(iMn,pull_requests.open); qh is shared urn/Xht, which appends encoded parameters to Ngt=/mcp-app. Thus the source-derived case-sensitive matcher is /mcp-app/connector_openai_code_review/pull_requests.open. ft selects codex only on that match and chatgpt otherwise; this is not the global product-mode store. Initializer execution order remains unverified.

Hosted inventory selects the _e provider for chatgpt, while another context requires Me and queries G with accountId, local host, empty roots and productContext. ct requires account, user and auth scope plus a matching hosted entrypoint app_id/tool_name. Missing data renders a loading/unavailable frame whose retry refetches that inventory; successful readiness delegates to lt.

Hosted launch uses an authenticated-user-enabled query keyed by hosted-mcp-extension, full descriptor and auth scope. It reads a cached conversation, fetches history with an abort listener, and recovers only conversation_deleted/history_disabled_conversation_expired. The launch request uses connectors://appId, cached thread or null, linkId, resource URI, tool name, empty toolInput, fullscreen and CODEX versus TPP SKU. Abort checks, listener removal, disabled retries and query lifecycle flags are explicit; service acceptance remains external.

The hosted adapter watches connected-link and inventory identity. A changed/missing entry or link schedules release in a microtask unless cleanup has canceled it. Cleanup removes the watcher and retention handle. Dispose first matches the current mcpAppId, then removes the exact query if the entry disappeared or resets it otherwise. These are source-level lifecycle contracts, not observed native disposal.

The hosted view builds fullscreen content, app context and conversation wrappers, handles self/global deep links with current-route identity checks, and supplies an adapter with openai/selfDeepLinks. A server-thread change writes the association. The storage key is hosted-mcp-conversations-v1; the entry identity is account/user/plugin/app/link/tool/resource, omitting productContext, while the launch query key includes the full descriptor. Logical shared cache use does not prove its physical authority or durability.

A recognized connection error with a nonempty connector ID offers Connect via the existing popup flow and optional reauthentication payload. Its AbortController is canceled on cleanup; a retry occurs only after didConnect and while not aborted. Pending/loading disables the button, errors are caught and pending is cleared in finally. This reuses the connection feature rather than proving a second OAuth implementation.

Retain the global-view goal and module as source-shared: it contains explicit Codex/ChatGPT hosted contexts and an independently selected app-server renderer. Retain the CODEX launch and its history/connection/lifecycle dependencies; do not delete conversation wrappers because their symbol or route-kind contains chatgpt. This does not prove all capabilities are shared or that the default hosted context is needed by every Codex entry.

Adopt distinct deep-link resolution and global-view display goals. FSC-0507 is settings-view selection, FSC-0123 is plugin detail, FSC-0132 owns the connection flow, and FSC-0413 opens an arbitrary clipboard deep link. Reuse those interfaces and do not duplicate settings, activation or OAuth implementations.
